reason: The text emphasizes hierarchical power structures through multiple elements: (1) Pharaoh is established as the supreme authority figure who gives binding commands ('וַיְצַ֣ו פַּרְעֹ֔ה לְכָל־ עַמּ֖וֹ' - 'Pharaoh commanded all his people'); (2) Clear power differentials are explicitly depicted between the Egyptian ruler and his people, and between Egyptians and Israelites; (3) The genealogical structure at the text's opening emphasizes family hierarchy and descent through the patrilineal line; (4) The narrative prominence given to Pharaoh's commands and their execution underscores the hierarchical relationship. While the text does not explicitly encourage hierarchy as a virtue or principle, it clearly emphasizes the hierarchical organization of Egyptian society and Pharaoh's unquestioned authority within it.
